messages:
incbot: ALERT: multiple node provisioning failures detected in us-west-2 — image pull errors from nvcr/nvidia registries. Severity: P1. Pager sent to oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/1844012300

kiran (oncall): seeing it — nodes stuck in ContainerCreating with imagePullBackOff. getting repeated 403/401 on nvcr pulls. sample from kubelet: 
```
Failed to pull image "nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to fetch oauth token: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized
```

maya (sre): confirming logs on provisioning queue — autoscaler failing to spin up gpu nodes because init container can't pull base image. A bunch of queued nodes for Dedicated pools.

sam (infra): initial hypothesis: NVCR token refresh endpoint returning 500s or rate-limited by NGC. I opened a vendor ticket (case 8773). pinging NVCR support now.

jess (eng): customer impact: some Dedicated pools (cust: algora) had burst provisioning during load test; provisioning delayed ~10-15min so API pods delayed start. Non-critical for most customers but one onboarding flow blocked.

kiran (oncall): mitigation plan — 1) fall back to our pre-pulled cache images on s3-backed registry mirror for new nodes 2) temporarily route provisioning to existing warm pool nodes 3) if needed, switch kubelet imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent via rollout for bootstrap DaemonSet (temp). Doing steps in that order.

maya (sre): executing step 2: enabling warm-pool scaleup for gp2-dedicated pool now (will add 6 nodes). Command: `./infractl pools scale --name gp2-dedicated --min 6 --max 12`

sam (infra): prepping mirror override. We have mirrors synced daily at gcr.io/redwood-mirror/nvcr/. Will patch provisioning bootstrap config to pull from `gcr.io/redwood-mirror/nvcr/cuda:11.8-runtime` while nvcr issue persists. Patch in progress.

kiran (oncall): doing on-call handoff to maya in 30m if stable. tagging ops-lead for customer comms. @ops-lead can you draft a short note for affected customers?

ops-lead: on it. Draft: "We're seeing delays in provisioning GPU nodes due to an upstream container registry authentication issue affecting NVIDIA's artifact service. We're routing new nodes to a verified mirror while the vendor resolves the outage. No action required — we will notify when normal provisioning resumes." Want me to send to customers in Dedicated onboarding?

jess (eng): please include estimated impact window (we think ~1-2 hours) and which customers might see delayed onboarding: algora, datafold, and one sandbox org (list attached).

registry-bot: Vendor status check: NVCR API status: https://status.nvidia.example — reported degraded performance in token service 18:12 UTC. Docker Hub status: green.

sam (infra): patch applied to bootstrap config in infra-repo: 
```yaml
# infra/provision/bootstrap.yaml (temp override)
image: gcr.io/redwood-mirror/nvcr/cuda:11.8-runtime
imagePullSecrets:
  - name: redwood-mirror-creds
```
kiran (oncall): restarting cloud-init/provisioner on warm nodes to pick up mirror settings. `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/provisioner`

maya (sre): monitoring node creation metrics: provisioning pipeline latency dropping from 14m -> 3m after warm-pool and mirror. partial mitigation successful.

kiran (oncall): still seeing ~1% of provisioning jobs hit 401 from nvcr when mirror not used (e.g., older bootstrap templates). Sam, can you run a one-off job to pre-pull all required images onto warm pool nodes?

sam (infra): launched job: `kubectl -n infra run image-prepull --image=alpine -- /bin/sh -c "docker pull gcr.io/redwood-mirror/nvcr/cuda:11.8-runtime && docker tag ..."` — will report when finished.

ops-lead: customer comms queued. Sending to Dedicated accounts and support queue now. Copy: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/OPS-1843

registry-bot: update from vendor: NVCR support: "We're investigating token service rate limits; temporary mitigation: use mirrored images or contact your account rep for elevated token limits."

jess (eng): noted. We should assess whether customers using private VPC installs are affected — private might not have mirror access. Maya, can we verify private deploys?

maya (sre): checked 3 private installs — two use private on-prem images (ok), one uses nvcr directly — alerted SE to coordinate with customer to pull mirror images into their registry.

kiran (oncall): escalation: if vendor doesn't resolve in 45m, prepare a controlled rollback of bootstrap templates cluster-wide to mirror images and mark as incident change. Sam, prepare the rollback PR and the canary plan.

sam (infra): PR ready in draft: `infra: temporary nvcr -> redwood-mirror override` includes kustomize patch and a rollback label. Canary planned on us-west-2 dev first (2 nodes), then prod.

maya (sre): metrics check: no customer-facing errors in API layer; most errors are infra-provisioning. Logging: increased 401 error count from 02:11 -> 02:30 UTC spike.

kiran (oncall): handoff to maya now — I'm going offline for a meeting. Maya, you're lead. I'll stay reachable for 15m.

maya (sre): taking over. continuing monitoring. updating incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.example/1844012300/postmortem-draft

ops-lead: customers notified. Support queue update: ticket templates added to speed ops responses.

registry-bot: vendor update: "Issue identified — token service overloaded by automated pulls; we deployed throttling rules which caused 401s for some tokens. Rolling back throttling now. ETA 30m."

maya (sre): if vendor fully rolls back throttling, we'll revert our temp overrides. Waiting for confirmation + stable metrics for 3 consecutive 5m windows.

sam (infra): prep for revert: PR to remove mirror override ready. will hold until maya gives green.

jess (eng): recommend we keep the mirror override in config but flag it as `ephemeral=false` so we can flip quickly if vendor flaps again. Also schedule a work item to reduce reliance on nvcr for critical bootstrap images.

maya (sre): vendor reports resolved at 18:48 UTC. I'm seeing nvcr 200 responses and provisioning success rates back to baseline.

kiran (oncall): (post-handoff) thanks team. I'll rejoin if anything else pops.

maya (sre): rolling back the bootstrap override now. `kubectl -n infra apply -f rollback-bootstrap-override.yaml`

sam (infra): rollback applied, canary nodes in dev still good. Proceeding to PROD rollback.

maya (sre): monitoring — provisioning latency steady ~2-4m. Closing active mitigations. Preparing timeline and action items for postmortem: 1) add mirror fallback to runbook 2) add metric alert for nvcr 401 spikes 3) pre-pull job for warm pools during high-burst windows 4) talk to vendor about quota/contract limits.

ops-lead: sending final customer note: "NVCR token service throttling briefly impacted GPU node provisioning. We routed to mirrors and warmed pools; vendor resolved the issue. Normal provisioning resumed. Reach out if you see residual issues." ✅

registry-bot: ticket update: NVCR support closed case 8773 — root cause: aggressive throttling following automated scan. Recommended long-term: customers use dedicated pull creds or mirror images.

maya (sre): incident marked resolved at 18:58 UTC. filing postmortem draft now. Thanks all. ☕
